A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JanusFlow. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original JanusFlow generation and understanding results, controlled ablations, and appendix analyses of resolution, guidance, and sampling steps.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports JanusFlow results on ChartQA and TextVQA in Table 5.

M1.justification: The architecture, decoupled encoders, three training stages, autoregressive and rectified-flow objectives, representation alignment, and generation procedure are unchanged. Revised training-step counts concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 5 add ChartQA and TextVQA, extending quantitative evaluation to dedicated chart-question-answering and image-text-reading benchmarks. Existing coverage is retained. The new dataset appendix names training sources already cited in v1.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Transfusion (7.3B) to the GenEval comparison. Table 5 adds LLaVA-NeXT and Qwen2-VL, both with 7B language models. Existing comparators remain; the newly cited MonoFormer is not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes Stage 2 warm-up from 0 to 2,000 steps and training duration from 380,000 to 390,000 steps. These are revisions to stated experimental settings; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 6 retains the same representation-alignment, encoder-decoupling, and task-specific-model ablations. The appendix resolution comparison, guidance and sampling sweeps, REPA training curves, and qualitative cases are also retained despite reordering.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-score and curve reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds JanusFlow scores of 64.6 on ChartQA and 55.5 on TextVQA, alongside additional comparator results. Table 2 newly reports Transfusion at 0.63, tying JanusFlow's retained GenEval score. Previously reported JanusFlow, ablation, and appendix scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained, including rectified-flow dynamics, training objectives, classifier-free guidance, and representation alignment. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: integrating autoregression with rectified flow, decoupling encoders, aligning representations, and achieving competitive understanding and generation with a compact model.

C2.justification: Interpretations of encoder decoupling, representation alignment, unified versus specialized training, and lower-resolution semantic control are unchanged. The added benchmark results receive no substantive new interpretation or limitation discussion.

D1.justification: New Appendix B explicitly lists pretraining datasets for understanding and generation, clarifying the citation-based description in Section 4.2. Table 1 revises two Stage 2 hyperparameters. Other implementation, preprocessing, hardware, and project-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL, ChartQA, TextVQA, and MonoFormer. Related work includes MonoFormer among similar approaches, while retaining the existing taxonomy and claimed architectural advantages.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short dataset appendix and cross-reference, reorders appendix material, and corrects the coauthor name Chenyue Wu to Chengyue Wu. The main narrative and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a comparator row; Table 5 gains two comparator rows and two benchmark columns with more compact typesetting. Table 6 moves from page 12 to page 11. Appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, with their plots and example images retained.

improvement.justification: The added ChartQA/TextVQA evaluations and relevant comparators make the empirical assessment more informative, while the dataset appendix improves clarity. These are limited gains: existing scores and mechanism ablations are retained, the training-schedule revisions are unexplained, and the added Transfusion tie at 0.63 is not reflected in the surrounding superiority wording. Overall, the broader evidence and clearer documentation support a modest quality improvement.
